title: Grid references & contours
examples: How do I read the numbers on a map?
What is the difference between a grid reference and a contour?
Can you show me how to find a point using both methods?

explain.say: Today we are learning about grid references and contour lines. These help us find exact places on a map. We will learn how to read both systems carefully.
A grid reference uses letters and numbers to pinpoint a spot. Think of it like giving an address on a street. It always needs two sets of coordinates.
Contour lines connect points of equal height above sea level. They look like lines drawn around hills. The closer the lines, the steeper the ground is.
To read relief, look at the pattern of the contour lines. If they are close together, the slope is very steep. If they are far apart, the ground is gentle.

draw.text: Close lines = Steep; Far lines = Gentle

explain.say: For a real-life example, imagine hiking in the mountains. You use contours to see where the steep parts are. You use grid references to tell your friends exactly where you are.
A common mistake is confusing the grid reference format. Remember it is always the Easting and the Northing, in that order. Always say the letters first.

faq.q: What is the difference between a grid reference and a coordinate pair?
faq.a: A grid reference is a specific system using letters and numbers on a map grid. A coordinate pair is a more general term for any two measurements, like latitude and longitude.
asks: Are grid references the same as coordinates?
What do I call the letters and numbers on a map?

faq.q: How do I tell if the ground is steep from the map?
faq.a: You look at the contour lines. If the lines are packed very closely together, it means the ground rises or falls very sharply. This indicates a steep slope.
asks: What do close contour lines mean?
How do I read steepness from contours?

faq.q: Do I need to know the scale to read a grid reference?
faq.a: While knowing the scale helps you understand the distance, the grid reference itself uses the map's established grid lines. You follow the grid pattern shown.
asks: Does the map scale change how I read the grid?
Is the grid reference always the same size?

faq.q: What do the numbers on a contour line mean?
faq.a: The number written on a contour line shows the exact height, or elevation, above sea level at that spot. For example, 200 metres means 200 metres high.
asks: What does the height number mean?

faq.q: If I see a contour line labelled 150 metres, what does that tell me?
faq.a: It tells you that every point on that specific line has the same height, which is 150 metres above sea level. It connects all points of equal height.
asks: What is the meaning of a contour value?
Does the line itself have a height?

facts: Grid references use a combination of letters and numbers found on a map grid.
Contour lines connect points that share the same elevation or height.
When contour lines are close together, the land has a steep gradient.
The unit of measurement for contour lines is usually metres or feet.

quiz.say: A map shows lines running across a hill at regular intervals of 10 metres. What do these lines represent?
quiz.why: Contour lines specifically connect points of the same elevation, which is what the description details.

wrong.0: Latitude lines measure north and south position, not height on a map.
wrong.1: Scale lines show distance measurement, but not constant height.
wrong.3: Grid lines are used for location coordinates, not for measuring height.

quiz.say: If a grid reference is given as 'C 456789', what does the 'C' most likely represent?
quiz.why: In standard grid referencing, the letter usually indicates the Easting (the horizontal position).

wrong.1: The letter usually marks the Easting, not the Northing.
wrong.2: The letter is part of the coordinate system, not a separate measurement factor.
wrong.3: The letter is part of the specific location reading, not the general map key.

quiz.say: You see contour lines that are very far apart from each other. What does this suggest about the terrain?

options.show: The ground is gentle or flat
options.say: The ground is gentle or flat

quiz.why: Wide spacing between contour lines means the height changes slowly over a large distance, indicating gentle ground.

wrong.1: Vertical ground would have lines touching or overlapping.
wrong.2: Rising quickly means the lines are packed very closely together.
wrong.3: The spacing itself is a valid piece of geographical data.
